title: Cabin air and vapour exposure
audience: Car detailers working with solvents and strong products inside vehicle cabins.
referencesAtStart: Official sources: Safe Work Australia, Workplace exposure standards for airborne contaminants (no date shown); Safe Work Australia, Hazardous chemicals register (no date shown).
learningOutcomes: Identify the vapour risk of solvent-rich products in a closed vehicle cabin.
Plan ventilation, exclusion and a safe re-entry decision for an interior treatment.
Refuse a solvent treatment in a closed, hot cabin without controls.

instruction.heading: Closed cabins concentrate vapour
instruction.body: A closed vehicle cabin, especially in hot weather, can concentrate the vapour from a solvent-rich stain remover. The vapour can irritate the eyes and airways, and can make people feel unwell. Before any interior treatment, check the product's SDS for vapour and ventilation requirements. Air concentrations at work must stay below the workplace exposure standard for each airborne contaminant, and the employer must monitor the air where needed to show that (Safe Work Australia, exposure standards, no date shown).

instruction.heading: Planning the treatment
instruction.body: Plan the interior treatment with ventilation, exclusion of people and pets, a chemical inventory and exposure controls. Set a safe re-entry time as the SDS and the plan direct, and do not re-enter a sealed cabin that still smells of solvent. An employee who plans to use a solvent in a closed cabin on a hot day is proposing an uncontrolled treatment, and it is refused until the controls are planned.

instruction.heading: Stop and record
instruction.body: Stop if the cabin cannot be ventilated, if someone becomes unwell, or if the product is not on the register. Record the proposal, the controls in place, the re-entry time and who approved it. A hazardous chemicals register kept at the workplace must list the current SDS for each chemical on it (Safe Work Australia, hazardous chemicals register, no date shown). The new workplace exposure limit list is due to take effect on 1 December 2026, so confirm which list applies on the day of the job (Safe Work Australia, exposure standards, no date shown).

procedure: Check the SDS for vapour and ventilation requirements before the treatment.
Plan ventilation, exclusion of people and pets, and the chemical inventory.
Set a safe re-entry time, and do not re-enter a cabin that still smells of solvent.
Refuse an uncontrolled solvent treatment in a closed, hot cabin.
Record the controls, the re-entry time and the approver.

workedExamples.situation: An employee plans to use a solvent-rich stain remover in a closed vehicle cabin during hot weather.
workedExamples.reasoning: Refuse the treatment as planned. Explain the vapour risk in a closed hot cabin, and require ventilation, exclusion, a chemical inventory and a re-entry time before any treatment. Record the proposal and the decision.

equipmentAndPpe: Product SDS with vapour and ventilation requirements.
Fans or open doors as the plan requires.
Respiratory protection only as the SDS requires, with a fit check.

commonErrors.error: Treating a closed cabin as a safe space for solvent.
Re-entering a cabin that still smells of solvent.
commonErrors.prevention: Wait for the set re-entry time and check.

commonErrors.error: Letting a pet or passenger into the treated cabin.
commonErrors.prevention: Exclude people and pets during and after the treatment.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Until the new workplace exposure limit list takes effect on 1 December 2026, the current workplace exposure standard list continues to apply (Safe Work Australia, exposure standards, no date shown).
A hazardous chemicals register kept at the workplace must list the current SDS for each chemical on it (Safe Work Australia, hazardous chemicals register, no date shown).
The SDS and the workplace exposure limits apply.

qualityStandard: Vapour risk identified and ventilation planned in the case study.
Re-entry time set and recorded in the practical.
documentationEvidence: Interior treatment plan with ventilation, exclusion and re-entry time.
summary: A closed hot cabin concentrates solvent vapour.
Plan ventilation, exclusion and a re-entry time from the SDS.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is a closed cabin a concern for solvent treatment?
options: It is cooler inside the cabin, so vapour does not matter
Vapour can concentrate and irritate or affect people
It is not a concern, since the cabin is sealed tight

knowledgeChecks.question: When is it safe to re-enter a treated cabin?
options: As soon as the spray dries on the surface and the smell has lifted
Whenever the client returns to the vehicle and wants to sit in it
At the re-entry time set in the plan, when it no longer smells of solvent

knowledgeChecks.question: What should happen to an uncontrolled solvent treatment in a closed hot cabin?
options: Refuse until ventilation, exclusion and a re-entry time are planned
Go ahead quickly, since the job is short and the cabin will air out
Use a fan only, pointed at the open door to keep the air moving
